He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon Ducks]] and the [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana Hoosiers]]. ==Early life and high school career== Kel’el Ware was born on April 20, 2004, in [[North Little Rock, Arkansas]], and attended [[North Little Rock High School]] from 2018 to 2022.{{cite web|first=Richard|last=Davenport|title=THE RECRUITING GUY: Ware keeps motor running on high|url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2021/may/07/ware-keeps-motor-running-on-high/|work=[[The Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]]|date=May 7, 2021|access-date=November 9, 2022}} As a junior, he averaged 16.2 points, 9.1 rebounds and 4.1 blocks per game. As a senior, Ware averaged 20.3 points, 12 rebounds and 5.7 blocks per game.{{cite web|first=Richard|last=Davenport|title=UA signees, Ware get all-star invite|url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2022/jan/26/ua-signees-ware-get-all-star-invite/|work=[[The Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]]|date=January 26, 2022|access-date=November 10, 2022}} He also played in the [[Jordan Brand Classic]], [[Nike Hoop Summit]] and the [[2022 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]] during his senior year.{{cite web|first=Nik|last=Streng|title=Future Oregon Duck Kel’el Ware to play in Nike Hoop Summit|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/highschoolsports/2022/04/future-oregon-duck-kelel-ware-to-play-in-nike-hoop-summit.html|work=[[The Oregonian]]|date=April 7, 2022|access-date=November 10, 2022}}{{cite web|first=Erick|last=Taylor|title=Arkansas connections galore at McDonald's game|url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2022/mar/29/arkansas-connections-galore-at-mcdonalds-game/|work=[[The Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]]|date=March 29, 2022|access-date=November 10, 2022}}{{cite 2022}} ===Recruiting=== Ware was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2022 class, according to major recruiting services.{{cite web|first=Andrew|last=Nemec|title=Updated rankings: Kel’el Ware, Oregon Ducks center signee, becomes consensus 5-star basketball prospect|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/recruiting/2022/01/updated-rankings-kelel-ware-oregon-ducks-center-signee-becomes-consensus-5-star-basketball-prospect.html|work=[[The Oregonian]]|date=January 19, 2022|access-date=November 9, 2022}} On August 9, 2021, he committed to playing college basketball for [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]] over offers from [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]], [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]], [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]], [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]], [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]], [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M]] and [[Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball|Texas Tech]].{{cite web|first=Chris|last=Hansen|title=Oregon Ducks land another 5-star recruit as 7–0 center Kel'el Ware commits|url=https://www.registerguard.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2021/08/09/oregon-ducks-land-another-5-star-recruit-7-0-center-kelel-ware-commits/5541311001|work=[[The Register Guard]]|date=August 9, 2021|access-date=November 9, 2022}} Ware was also offered a two-year contract for $900,000 from [[Overtime Elite]], but he declined the offer and maintained his commitment to Oregon.{{cite web|first=Andrew|last=Nemec|title=Kel’el Ware, Oregon Ducks 5-star center pledge, declines $900,000 offer from Overtime Elite, remains committed: = 8 | accessdate = November 11, 2022 | bball = yes }} ==College career== Ware entered his freshman season at Oregon as the Ducks' second center.{{cite web|first=Matt|last=Prehm|title=Dana Altman sees talent but also lots of room for improvement in newcomers Kel'el Ware, Keeshawn Barthelemy|url=https://247sports.com/college/oregon/Article/Oregon-Ducks-basketball-Kelel-Ware-Keeshawn-Barthelemy-197216052/|work=[[247Sports]]|date=November 9, 2022|access-date=November 9, 2022}} He also entered the season as a potential first-round selection in the [[2023 NBA draft]].{{cite web|first=Jeff|last=Borzello|title=Newcomer Impact Rankings: Which men's college basketball freshmen, transfers will lead teams in 2022–23?|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/insider/story/_/id/34918359|website=ESPN.com|date=November 2, 2022|access-date=November 10, 2022}} After averaging 26 minutes played, 10.3 points, 5.6 rebounds and 1.4 blocks over the first nine games of the season, Ware saw a decline in playing time due to what Oregon's coaching staff believed to be an inconsistent work ethic.{{cite web|first=James|last=Crepea|title=Oregon men’s basketball center Kel’el Ware to enter transfer portal|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/ducks/2023/03/oregon-mens-basketball-center-kelel-ware-to-enter-transfer-portal.html|work=[[The Oregonian]]|date=March 27, 2023|access-date=March 27, 2023}} He ultimately averaged 6.6 points and 4.1 rebounds per game on the season. At the end of the season, Ware entered the NCAA transfer portal.{{cite web|first=Jeff|last=Borzello|title=Oregon's Kel'el Ware, former top-10 recruit, to enter portal|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/35970015|website=ESPN.com|date=March 27, 2023|access-date=March 27, 2023}} Ware ultimately transferred to [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]].{{cite web|first=Jeff|last=Borzello|title=Oregon center Kel'el Ware transferring to Indiana|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/36151417|website=ESPN.com|date=April 10, 2023|access-date=April 11, 2023}} He started at center in the Hoosiers' season-opener against [[2023–24 Florida Gulf Coast Eagles men's basketball team|Florida Gulf Coast]] and recorded the first [[double-double]] of his college career with 13 points, 12 rebounds, four assists, three blocks and two steals as Indiana won 69–63.{{cite web|title=Indiana basketball beats FGCU thanks to Kel'el Ware, Gabe Cupps debuts|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/college/indiana/2023/11/07/indiana-basketball-beats-fgcu-score-kelel-ware-gabe-cupps-debuts-iu-hoosiers-florida-gulf-coast/71473465007/|work=[[Indianapolis Star]]|date=November 7, 2023|access-date=November 9, 2023}} Ware set a new career high with 22 points scored while also grabbing 12 rebounds on November 16, 2023, in a 89–80 victory over [[2023–24 Wright State Raiders men's basketball team|Wright State]].{{cite web|title=Kel'el Ware came to IU with point to prove. He's playing like it, and Hoosiers need it.|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/college/indiana/2023/11/17/indiana-hoosiers-basketball-kelel-ware-playing-with-point-to-prove-iu-mike-woodson-oregon-transfer/71550763007/|work=[[Indianapolis Star]]|date=November 17, 2023|access-date=November 17, 2023}} He re-set his career high in scoring with 28 points in a 89–76 win over [[2023–24 Harvard Crimson men's basketball team|Harvard]].{{cite web|title=Career games for Ware and Mgbako lead Indiana past Harvard 89-76|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401577615|work=[[ESPN]]|date=November 26, 2023|access-date=November 27, 2023}} After the season, Ware declared for the [[2024 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{cite web |last=Glenesk |first=Matthew |date=March 26, 2024 |title=Indiana basketball sophomore Kel'el Ware declares for 2024 NBA draft |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/college/indiana/2024/03/26/indiana-basketball-kelel-ware-declares-for-2024-nba-draft-iu-hoosiers/72930443007/ |access-date=March 26, 2024 |work=[[Indianapolis Star]]}} ==Professional career== === Miami Heat (2024–2026) === Ware was selected with the 15th overall pick by the [[Miami Heat]] in the [[2024 NBA draft]]{{cite web|first=Zachary|last=Weinberger|title=Why the Heat is the ‘perfect place’ for Kel’el Ware|url=https://clutchpoints.com/heat-news-why-miami-is-perfect-place-for-kelel-ware|website=ClutchPoints|date=June 26, 2024|access-date=June 26, 2024}} and on July 2, 2024, he signed with the Heat.{{cite web|title=HEAT SIGN KEL’EL WARE |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-sign-kelel-ware|website=NBA.com|date=July 2, 2024|access-date=July 2, 2024}} Ware was named Eastern Conference Rookie of the Month for January 2025.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/kelel-ware-named-eastern-conference-rookie-of-the-month|title=KEL’EL WARE NAMED EASTERN CONFERENCE ROOKIE OF THE MONTH|website=NBA.com|date=February 24, 2025|access-date=March 5, 2026}} On November 11, 2025, Ware put up a career-high 20 rebounds in a 140–138 overtime win over the [[2025–26 Cleveland Cavaliers season|Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/heats-kelel-ware-pulls-down-career-high-20-rebounds/|title=Heat's Kel'el Ware: Pulls down career-high 20 rebounds|website=CBS Sports|date=November 11, 2025|access-date=March 5, 2026}} On December 21, Ware put up a career-high 28 points, along with 19 rebounds, in a 132–125 loss to the [[2025–26 New York Knicks season|New York Knicks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/coups-takeaways-heat-hot-knicks-hotter-brunson-ware-122125|title=Coup’s Takeaways: HEAT Get Hot, Knicks Get Hotter As Brunson Earns The Win On Ware’s Career Night|website=NBA.com|last=Moorhead|first=Couper|date=December 21, 2025|access-date=March 5, 2026}} On March 5, 2026, Ware put up 16 points, 11 rebounds, a career-high seven blocks and five steals in a 126–110 win over the [[2025–26 Brooklyn Nets season|Brooklyn Nets]]. He became the first player to put up a 10-10-5-5 game in Heat franchise history and the first to do so off the bench in NBA history.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/miami-heat/heat-news-kelel-ware-makes-unthinkable-nba-history-in-dominant-win-over-nets|title=Heat’s Kel’el Ware makes unthinkable NBA history in dominant win over Nets|website=ClutchPoints|last=Weinberger|first=Zachary|date=March 5, 2026|access-date=March 5, 2026}}{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/heats-kelel-ware-monster-stat-line-thursday/|title=Heat's Kel'el Ware: Monster stat line Thursday|website=CBS Sports|date=March 5, 2026|access-date=March 5, 2026}} On April 4, Ware recorded 24 points, 19 rebounds and seven blocks in a 152–136 victory over the [[2025–26 Washington Wizards season|Washington Wizards]].{{Cite web|title=Heat's Kel'el Ware Dominates vs. Wizards Weeks After Bam Adebayo's Stunning 83-Point Game|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/25414707-heats-kelel-ware-dominates-vs-wizards-weeks-after-bam-adebayos-stunning-83-point-game|access-date=June 23, 2026|website=bleacherreport.com|language=en|date=April 5, 2026|last=Kasabian|first=Paul}} === Milwaukee Bucks (2026–present) === On July 6, 2026, Ware, alongside [[Tyler Herro]], [[Kasparas Jakučionis]], [[Jaime Jaquez Jr.]], the rights to [[Nate Ament]] and four future draft picks, was traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in exchange for [[Giannis Antetokounmpo]] and [[Bobby Portis]].{{Cite web |date=July 6, 2026 |title=Heat acquire Giannis Antetokounmpo in blockbuster deal |url=https://www.nba.com/news/reports-heat-acquire-giannis-antetokounmpo-in-blockbuster-deal |access-date=July 6, 2026 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} ==National team career== Ware played for the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States under-18 basketball team]] at the [[2022 FIBA Under-18 Americas Championship]].{{cite web|first=James|last=Crepea|title=Oregon signee Kel’el Ware to play for USA Basketball’s U18 men’s national team|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/ducks/2022/06/oregon-signee-kelel-ware-to-play-for-usa-basketballs-u18-mens-national-team.html|work=[[The Oregonian]]|date=June 3, 2022|access-date=November 10, 2022}} He was named to the All-Tournament team after averaging 15.7 points, 6.8 rebounds and 1.8 blocks as the United States won the gold medal.{{cite web|first=James|last=Crepea|title=Oregon signee Kel’el Ware, USA Basketball’s U18 men’s national team win gold at Americas Championship|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/ducks/2022/06/oregon-signee-kelel-ware-usa-basketballs-u18-mens-national-team-win-gold-at-americas-championship.html|work=[[The Oregonian]]|date=June 13, 2022|access-date=November 9, 2022}} ==Personal life== Ware is the son of Tamika and Cedrick Spaight (stepfather).{{cite web |title=Kel'el Ware Q&A |url=https://www.prospectiveinsight.com/post/kelel-ware |access-date=15 February 2025 |website=ProspectiveInsight.com |quote="My real dad is 6’6” and my mom’s dad was 6’6” too."}} He has two brothers, Javarus Ware and Kashis Spaight and two sisters, Dyamyn Ware and Jazzmyn Spaight.{{cite web|title=Kel'el Ware - Men's Basketball|url=https://iuhoosiers.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/kel-el-ware/17643|work=Indiana University Athletics|access-date=July 26, 2024}} His mother named him after [[Superman]]'s Kryptonian name, Kal-El.{{Cite web |title=Kel’el Ware: “My mom named me after Superman” |url=https://www.talkbasket.net/198297-kelel-ware-my-mom-named-me-after-superman |website=TalkBasket.net |date=June 27,
